title: Effect of Platelet-Rich Plasma on Marginal Bone Loss and Peri-Implant Bone Density as Analysed by CBCT: An Exploratory Randomized Controlled Trial
html: Introduction Dental implants are a predictable and highly successful treatment modality for the rehabilitation of edentulous spaces. Preservation of peri-implant bone is critical to the long-term success of dental implants. Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP), an autologous source of growth factors, may enhance early osseointegration and bone stability. Aim To evaluate the effect of autologous PRP on marginal bone loss (MBL) and peri-implant bone density (PIBD) over a 3-month period using Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT). Materials and Methods This exploratory split-mouth randomized controlled clinical trial included 23 patients (46 implant sites). Implant sites within each patient were randomly allocated to PRP-treated and control groups. Patients were unaware of which implant site received PRP, and outcome assessment was performed by a blinded examiner. PRP was prepared using a double-spin method and applied to the implant surface. CBCT scans assessed MBL and PIBD at baseline and 3 months. ISQ (Implant Stability Quotient) was measured with resonance frequency analysis (RFA). Data normality was assessed using the Shapiro–Wilk test. Depending on data distribution, paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used for paired comparisons, and Friedman test was used for repeated non-parametric comparisons. Results At 3 months, PRP-treated implant sites demonstrated significantly greater peri-implant bone density at the coronal, middle, and apical thirds and better preservation of marginal bone levels compared with control sites. Implant stability (ISQ) was significantly higher in the PRP group than in the control group at 3 months; however, within-group changes from baseline were not statistically significant. Conclusion Within the limitations of this exploratory randomized clinical trial, autologous PRP was associated with reduced marginal bone loss and increased relative peri-implant radiographic density during the early healing period.
